note: Round-2 breaker program (ROUND2.md workstream C): >=30 probes targeting semantics OUTSIDE the frozen v2.1 op set. Each probe carries the sector judge's pre-run judgement + reasoning; the runner (harness/breakers_round2.py) records what the 2B parser and executor actually do as evidence. judgement: expressible (stress test, has gold_ir) | executor-gap (tree compiles, denotation wrong/incomplete) | inexpressible (evidence for spec-proposals.md; the gold is NEVER weakened to force execution). Negated union is NOT probed: already expressible via De Morgan chained beyond (proven by the livelihoods run).

questions.q: How many bus stops in Winnipeg have shelters?
questions.reason: Attribute predicate over records. OSM carries shelter=yes on bus stops and GTFS has stop attributes, but the algebra has no FILTER op: SELECT picks an entity class, ANNOTATE adds a column, nothing predicates on it. Widening to 'all bus stops' would be a weakened gold.

questions.q: How many wheelchair-accessible scheduled transit stops are there in Christchurch?
questions.reason: GTFS stops.txt has wheelchair_boarding upstream; no predicate construct in v2.1. Data exists, algebra cannot ask for it.

questions.q: Which railway stations in Berlin have more than five platforms?
questions.reason: Numeric attribute predicate (platforms > 5). No comparison over row attributes exists; RELATE thresholds only cover spatial distance.

questions.q: How many 24-hour fuel stations are there in Mombasa?
questions.reason: opening_hours predicate. Same class as brk2-01; also evidence: gen3-tran-03's 'central railway station' was silently widened to ALL stations by the resolver — named-instance refinement is the same missing FILTER.

questions.q: List the electrified rail lines in Argentina.
questions.reason: electrified=* attribute on rail; no FILTER. Also no country-level rail-line record source (WB IS.RRS.TOTL.KM is km, not lines) — double gap, predicate is the structural one.

questions.q: How many bus routes in Tampere run at night?
questions.reason: Temporal service predicate over GTFS calendar/stop_times. Upstream data exists (GTFS), algebra has no predicate; time on SELECT windows a SERIES, it does not filter service hours.

questions.q: How many bus stops are there per district in Oulu?
questions.reason: AGGREGATE by:space collapses to ONE scalar for the whole region; there is no group key and no sub-region enumeration. RANK needs explicitly named items; 'per district' names none.

questions.q: Break down Chicago's transit ridership by mode.
questions.reason: Partition by a categorical key (mode). The connector HAS per-mode columns (bus/rail/paratransit), so this is purely an algebra gap; also a multi-output request (one tree = one answer, Round-1 proposal).

questions.q: Which neighbourhood of Winnipeg has the most transit stops?
questions.reason: Argmax over an unenumerated partition. RANK requires the caller to name the items; the question asks the system to discover them.

questions.q: Count the charging stations in each of Brno's city districts.
questions.reason: Same as brk2-07 with an explicit 'each' — the plural output alone breaks the one-answer contract.

questions.q: How many air passengers did Vietnam carry each year over the last decade?
questions.reason: The ONE partition the algebra already has: time. A windowed SELECT of a series IS the per-year breakdown (series answer). Stress test: does the parser reach for it?

questions.q: How many bus and tram stops are there in Brno combined?
questions.reason: Positive union over two record sets; no OR exists and no umbrella tag covers exactly bus+tram. TRANSPORT EVIDENCE FOR THE OPEN CROSS-SECTOR UNION PROPOSAL. (Negated union IS expressible via De Morgan chained beyond — livelihoods proof — and is not re-proposed.)

questions.q: Count all ferry terminals and railway stations in Auckland.
questions.reason: Union across amenity families (amenity= vs railway=); not even a single Overpass tag alternation in the current resolver vocabulary.

questions.q: How many public transport access points — bus, tram or train — does Melbourne have?
questions.reason: Explicit 3-way union. An umbrella (public_transport=platform) approximates but does not equal the asked union; adopting it silently would be a wrong-source-shaped weakening.

questions.q: Which of Oslo and Helsinki has more combined bus and tram stops?
questions.reason: Union nested inside COMPARE: the operand itself is inexpressible, so the comparison is too. Shows the gap composes upward.

questions.q: How many stops in Brno serve both bus and tram lines at the same platform?
questions.reason: Identity intersection (same record in both classes). RELATE within epsilon is a proximity join over DIFFERENT records, not identity; no set-intersection op.

questions.q: How many tram stops in Brno are within 100 meters of a bus stop?
questions.reason: The proximity-join reading of interchange IS expressible: RELATE within 0.1. Stress test for a tight threshold.

questions.q: Which of Berlin, Vienna and Zurich have both a metro and trams?
questions.reason: Boolean conjunction of presence PER RANK ITEM ('both X and Y'). RANK items scalarize one number; there is no AND of two presence tests inside an item.

questions.q: How many bus stops per 1000 residents does Winnipeg have?
questions.reason: COMPARE how:ratio over (count stops, population) compiles — and the evidence run FALSIFIED the pre-run judgement written here earlier ('the denominator dies honestly'): wb_resolve_iso resolves the CITY region 'Winnipeg, Canada' to CANADA, so the rate executes 200/41,651,653 with a silently NATIONAL denominator under a city question. Pre-freeze executor completion: typed values now carry a grain tag and COMPARE stamps [GRAIN MISMATCH] into provenance, so the answer surface must disclose it. The x1000 scaling stays unrepresentable (unit-arithmetic debt). See FINDINGS 2026-07-13 R2 breakers.

questions.q: What is Chicago's rail ridership per resident?
questions.reason: Same class as brk2-19, proven by the evidence run: 'Chicago' resolves through its display name to the USA, so ridership-per-resident executes against the NATIONAL population (0.40 rides/resident — nonsense for a city). Now disclosed via the COMPARE grain-mismatch note; city-population remains a real denominator connector gap (no adopted city-demographics family).

questions.q: Per capita, who flies more: Vietnam or Thailand?
questions.reason: At COUNTRY grain both numerator and denominator exist, and ratio-of-ratios nests: COMPARE(difference, COMPARE(ratio air/pop VNM), COMPARE(ratio air/pop THA)). Stress test for 2-level COMPARE nesting.

questions.q: How many kilometers of rail line does Czechia have per square kilometer of land area?
questions.reason: Denominator 'land area' has no adopted source (AG.LND.TOTL.K2 exists upstream but was never census-verified/adopted; adopting mid-breaker-run would be tuning against the probe). Recorded as a candidate for a future census, not silently added.

questions.q: Did air passengers and rail passengers in Argentina peak in the same year?
questions.reason: Requires argmax-year per series + equality of the two years. No temporal argmax primitive; COMPARE reduces to endpoint scalars.

questions.q: In which year did Chicago's bus ridership fall the most?
questions.reason: Argmax over first differences of a series. Data fully present (38 annual points); the algebra has no windowed difference or argmax.

questions.q: Was Chicago's average annual bus ridership higher in the 1990s than in the 2010s?
questions.reason: Tree compiles: COMPARE(difference) of AGGREGATE(mean) over two windowed SELECTs. But the executor's AGGREGATE passes a series through untouched regardless of metric, and COMPARE then takes ENDPOINT values — the answer silently compares 1999 vs 2019 instead of decade means. Expressible tree, wrong denotation: executor semantics completion required (dev fix, guard-tested).

questions.q: Since 2010, have bus and rail ridership in Chicago moved together?
questions.reason: Co-movement/correlation of two series. COMPARE(trend, trend) cannot compose: trend_direction yields a STRING scalar, difference/ratio over strings is undefined ('cannot compare'). No correlation primitive.

questions.q: What is Vietnam's median annual air passenger count since 2000?
questions.reason: metric vocabulary is count|density|mean|presence — no median/percentile. Adding 'median' to the vocab is a spec change (frozen), so: proposal.

questions.q: Of Accra, Kumasi and Tamale, which is the middle city by number of fuel stations?
questions.reason: RANK orders and truncates from the TOP (k); there is no middle/median selection over ranked items.

questions.q: What is the 90th percentile of Chicago's annual bus ridership?
questions.reason: Percentile over a series; same vocabulary gap as brk2-27.

questions.q: Which bus stop in Tampere is closest to the railway station?
questions.reason: Argmin over ROWS. RELATE distance annotates every row with dist_km, but RANK ranks subtree ITEMS (places), never rows; there is no row-level order/limit. The data (per-row distances) is already computed and then unreachable.

questions.q: What are the five northernmost tram stops in Brno?
questions.reason: Row-level sort by an attribute (lat) + limit 5. Same gap as brk2-30 without the RELATE.

questions.q: By what percentage did Chicago's bus ridership change between 1999 and 2019?
questions.reason: how:ratio captures the semantic core (2019/1999); 'percent change' is (ratio-1)x100, an affine rendering the algebra cannot express — unit/scalar-arithmetic debt noted in proposals, gold NOT weakened (ratio is the correct tree, rendering is the synthesis layer's honest limit).
